ENGAGEMENT TYPE: Nonprofit Organization (501(c)(3)) — GAGAS (Yellow Book) + Single Audit (2 CFR 200)

FINDINGS:
1. Client Entity — Not Identified
   Severity: High
   Risk: The workpaper cannot be linked to a specific engagement without a client name, undermining the audit file's evidentiary value.

2. GAGAS / Yellow Book Applicability — Not Documented (§Q2)
   Severity: High
   Risk: Failure to document GAGAS applicability may cause the engagement to omit Yellow Book independence, CPE, and reporting requirements. Applicable standards: GAS §3.36.

3. Grant Compliance Audit — Scope Not Documented (§Q1(b))
   Severity: Medium
   Risk: Unrecorded grant compliance scope may result in omitted federal award testing required under the Uniform Guidance. Applicable standards: 2 CFR 200.514; 2 CFR 200.516.

4. Engagement Partner Sign-Off Date — Missing (§5)
   Severity: Medium
   Risk: The absence of a partner sign date prevents independence dating verification required under the applicable engagement standards. Applicable standards: AU-C 220; ET 1.110.010; GAS §3.36.

5. Form Preparation Date — Not Documented
   Severity: Medium
   Risk: Without a preparation date, the timeliness of the engagement form completion cannot be verified against engagement deadlines. Applicable standards: AU-C 230.

6. Preparer Id
   Severity: Medium
   Risk: This documentation deficiency weakens the evidentiary basis of the engagement workpaper and should be corrected prior to report issuance.

7. Reporting Framework — Not Documented (§Q1(a))
   Severity: High
   Risk: Without a documented reporting framework (GAAP / GASB / special purpose), the basis of accounting cannot be confirmed or disclosed appropriately. Applicable standards: AU-C 700.

8. Reviewer Id
   Severity: Medium
   Risk: This documentation deficiency weakens the evidentiary basis of the engagement workpaper and should be corrected prior to report issuance.

RECOMMENDATION:
Management of this Nonprofit Organization (501(c)(3)) should implement corrective procedures to address the 8 identified documentation deficiencies. As a nonprofit entity, corrective actions must address donor restrictions, board oversight requirements, and Form 990 filing obligations. All corrections should be completed and documented prior to report issuance in accordance with Government Auditing Standards (Yellow Book) and 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance).
